reconcile.note: Clarke denies that the unequally-yoked warning of 2 Corinthians 6:14 targets marriage, keeping it separate from his counsel to remain with an unbelieving spouse.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Hans Dieter Betz catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Hans Dieter Betz, "2 Cor 6:14-7:1: An Anti-Pauline Fragment?" Journal of Biblical Literature 92 (1973).

sides.snippet: if any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she is content to live with him, let him not leave her
sides.verseText: But to the rest I--not the Lord--say, if any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she is content to live with him, let him not leave her.

sides.snippet: Don't be unequally yoked with unbelievers, for what fellowship have righteousness and iniquity?
sides.verseText: Don't be unequally yoked with unbelievers, for what fellowship have righteousness and iniquity? Or what communion has light with darkness?
